conbody.p: HP large-format printers support several driver options for Windows and macOS, each suited to different workflow requirements. Selecting the correct driver ensures reliable connectivity, accurate color output, and full access to printer features.

section.title: HP DesignJet Printer Driver
section.p: The HP DesignJet printer driver integrates the printer as a standard system printer in Windows or macOS. Once installed, users can print to the device from any application using the operating system print dialog. The driver exposes print-quality presets, paper type selection, color management profiles, and scaling options.

ul.li: Supported on Windows 10/11 (64-bit) and macOS 12 or later.
Install via the HP Support website or the HP Smart app.
Supports PostScript and HP-PCL job languages depending on the printer model.

section.title: HP Click Printing Software
section.p: HP Click is a free, lightweight desktop application designed for direct file submission to HP large-format printers without requiring a full RIP. It is the recommended driver for simple sign and display workflows.

ul.li: Accepts PDF, TIFF, JPEG, and HP-GL/2 file formats.
Provides quicksets for common substrates and print-quality combinations.
Installs a virtual system printer (HP Click Driver) that lets users print from any application via the OS print dialog.
Available for Windows 10/11 and macOS 12 or later.

section.title: RIP Software Drivers
section.p: For production environments requiring advanced color management, nesting, or tiling, third-party RIP software (such as SAi FlexiPRINT, Onyx, or Caldera) connects to the printer via its IP address or USB. RIP drivers offer the most precise control over ink density, color profiling, and media profiles.
section.note: Always download printer drivers from the official HP Support website to ensure driver authenticity and compatibility with the current firmware version.
